coherence.spoken_as: I asked myself one question: what if there's a 5% chance I am an idiot? First thing you do is no. You say no, you continue, you proceed. I'm an idiot — of course I'm not. But what if. I could do better at managing my business. I reacted with a no. Managing the business, talking to friends, communication, studying — all of these are me giving myself a chance to respond. When I gave myself a chance to respond, I realized there's a whole lot that was happening.

shorts.title: Focus vs Tunnel Vision

situation.statement: When you start with focus it becomes tunnel vision.
situation.pressure: You want to finish what you started, but what you started no longer looks like you thought and it's no longer contributing. It didn't work.
situation.resolve: Keep track: write the thought down, capture where it came from — that gives a different perspective, so you don't revive the loop.

shorts.overlay_notes: Last heard clause must be keep track, not revive the loop. Loop is pressure. Do not play 58:52–58:56 (fucked up way).

coherence.spoken_as: When you start with focus it becomes tunnel vision. You want to finish what you started. What you started no longer looks like you thought — it didn't work. We were working towards something people were not responding to, so we stopped. You question yourself, feel depressed, and three weeks later go back to the same question and revive that loop. As you do that you have to keep track. I'd think of something and I'd write a note. I was able to capture the thoughts that enter my head and consider where they came from. It gave me a different perspective.

resolution.text: There's a transitional period where you're looking at the new house and thinking what's the new stuff you want to build. Which is basically right now.
